topic: Motion Graphs and Ticker Tape Diagrams
key_concepts: Motion is a change in position over time
Motion can be represented visually by motion graphs and tape charts
Slope of a line equals rise over run, or change in y over change in x
Horizontal lines have zero slope; upward-slanting lines have positive slope; downward-slan
Steeper lines indicate larger slope; curved lines indicate changing slope
In position-time graphs, time is on the x-axis and position on the y-axis
Distance-time graphs plot distance traveled against time; displacement-time graphs plot di
A horizontal line on a distance-time graph indicates the object is stationary
A straight diagonal line sloping upward on a distance-time graph indicates constant speed
A curve sloping upward on a distance-time graph indicates increasing speed
A horizontal line on a speed-time graph indicates speed is not changing over time
Ticker tape diagrams use dot spacing to represent motion; equal spacing indicates constant
